When you visit a website, your computer doesn't have to make a long trip to the internet every single time you refresh the page. If you check the website again quickly, it might just serve the cached data instead of sending a new request to the internet.

If the website changes its name or the connection goes down, that timer can help the system decide whether to update the cache or clear it entirely. Essentially, this mechanism speeds up page loading and reduces the strain on the network by reusing old information for a set period.
